items.passage:
Speed and Capacity Are the Only Real Agent Differentiators Now

My guess is that Instinct slowed down because it has to manage its inference costs. It’s free to use, so the company is unlikely to be earning any revenue. The business is likely funded entirely on venture capital, and people like me use it at an unbelievable clip.

Big Tech Has a Structural Advantage

A massively profitable business subsidizing a massively unprofitable AI business is a real advantage, at least in the short term.

source_piece.title: A Few Slow Hours Were All It Took to Make Me Cheat on My AI Agent

hook.headline: Instinct users say they've noticed a slowdown with the buzzy AI agent

platform_cuts.linkedin:
Business Insider reports Instinct users have noticed slower answers and task completion. I had a few slow hours myself and tried Muse. Instinct has bounced back, but the episode sharpened my view.

Speed and capacity are the only real agent differentiators now. My guess is that Instinct slowed down because it has to manage inference costs. I don’t know that for sure. It’s free to use, and people like me use it at an unbelievable clip.

A massively profitable business subsidizing a massively unprofitable AI business is a real advantage, at least in the short term. But I still find Instinct easier to use. That’s why I came back.

items.passage: Step three is ownership, and this is where most companies are flying blind. The organizations figuring this out have an AI lead who is AI-native, or close to it, overseeing usage across the company. When AI lives inside the legacy IT department, you get process and compliance. Experimentation and cost discipline come from giving it its own home.

backlog.passage: AI is better at what executives do than what employees do. This might be the most important point. Executives spend most of their time making decisions and communicating, exactly what large language models excel at. Employees, on the other hand, make the products and services the company sells. AI is dramatically better at helping you talk, write, and choose between options than it is at actually creating things.

backlog.passage: I jumped to Muse as soon as Instinct started acting up. Up until then, Instinct felt sticky. It knew my requests, understood what I wanted, and was working through a long list of my projects. But AI isn’t a person. Getting a new one up to speed doesn’t take long. Nothing locks me into either agent. When LLMs went mainstream a few years ago, I argued that these models would quickly become commoditized, and the real advantage would be something like proprietary data. For an agent working as my assistant, the proprietary data is mine. I can hand that to any agent.
